info.description:
Timeline REST API. Implements technical specification v0.8:
accounts and invites, events and stages, participant assignments,
registration with self-reported status, reminder rules and the audit log.

The system does not verify the external registration site: the status is self-reported
by the user or set administratively.

Authentication is cookie-based: the access token lives 15 minutes, the refresh token
rotates and lives 30 days. Every mutating request must send
a CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header; obtain one from GET /auth/csrf.
All timestamps are transferred in UTC using RFC 3339.
info.title: Timeline API

get.description: Restricted to administrators. Entries are immutable; file export is not supported in the MVP.
Administrative list with every state, search and filters.

post.description: The event is created unpublished; end_at must be later than start_at.

get.description: Administrative read, including notes.

patch.description:
Changing end_at increments the registration schedule_version, cancels stale
pending notifications and triggers reconciliation. Violating the condition
deadline_at <= end_at is rejected.

409.description: the registration deadline falls outside end_at

post.description: Terminal state in the MVP: pending notifications are cancelled and no new ones are created.

parameters.description: Include participants removed from the roster
parameters.name: include_removed

post.description:
Re-adding a previously removed participant reactivates the record and increments
assignment_version. The assignment, registration status, primary notification and audit
entry run in a single transaction per participant; the result is returned per entry.

requestBody.description: List of users and their roles

post.description: Moves participation to REMOVED and cancels pending notifications. Sent ones are preserved.

Only assigned participants are copied. The participant role is copied as a value
by default and can be overridden. Existing participants are skipped
and returned as separate result entries.
post.summary: Copy the roster from another event

post.description:
The event becomes visible to participants and the scheduler; deferred primary
notifications are created by reconciliation.

409.description: the event is already published or archived

post.description:
Creating an active registration creates missing TODO statuses for every assigned
participant. Primary notifications are created only for a published, non-archived
event; otherwise they are deferred until publication. The deadline must satisfy
the condition deadline_at <= event.end_at.

409.description: registration already exists or the deadline falls outside end_at

patch.description:
Changing the link increments notification_content_version; changing the deadline increments
schedule_version. In both cases pending notifications are cancelled and current ones
are created by reconciliation with a new logical key.

post.description: Only TODO and NOT_REQUIRED are accepted. The result is returned per participant.
Returns the number of records to be changed and skipped without modifying data.
Pending notifications are cancelled; statuses are preserved but stop being actionable.

Increments activation_version and schedule_version and creates missing statuses;
participants in TODO receive the primary notification again.

The sign of offset_minutes selects the type: a positive value is a reminder before the deadline,
zero fires at the deadline, and a negative value is an overdue notification.
A registration accepts at most 10 rules.

409.description: a rule with this offset already exists or the slot limit is reached

post.description:
Overlapping stages and stages outside the event period are allowed.
A stage produces no notifications.

Creation is serialised by normalised email: a previous unaccepted invite is revoked,
then a new one is created. An invite for an existing user address is rejected with a conflict
regardless of that user's activity.

409.description: a user with this email already exists

post.description:
Returns participation to ASSIGNED, increments assignment_version, clears removed_at
and sets the role again. An existing registration status is preserved.

patch.description: team_role is a free-text role on the event, not an access permission.

get.description: Participants in TODO whose deadline has passed while the event has not finished.

Share of assigned participants who have self-reported registration across every
published, non-archived event with an ACTIVE registration. The system never checks
the external site: DONE means the participant said so, NOT_REQUIRED means an
administrator waived the requirement, and both count as covered. When no event
requires registration the aggregate is not applicable and share is omitted rather
than reported as zero.
Participants in TODO whose deadline falls within the given window.

delete.description:
The rule is set to enabled=false; the row is preserved so that the occupied slot
and offset stay reserved.

patch.description:
Changing schedule fields increments schedule_version once per transaction
and triggers notification reconciliation.

Allowed transitions: TODO to DONE, DONE to TODO, TODO/DONE to NOT_REQUIRED,
NOT_REQUIRED to TODO. Entering TODO increments todo_cycle and clears registered_at.

get.description:
Returns the text a recipient would receive for one registration status: the subject,
the body, the channel that the rules of specification section 10 would pick and the
moment the entry would be scheduled for.

The call has no side effects at all. No notification row is created, no logical_key is
claimed and no deduplication state is touched, no provider is contacted and nothing
reaches the audit log. Calling it twice changes nothing and never suppresses a real
notification that the scheduler is about to create.

The text is rendered in the recipient's own language taken from their profile, not in
the language of the administrator asking: the point of a preview is to show what the
recipient will read.

Pass rule_id to preview a reminder or an overdue notice; the type follows the sign of
the rule offset. Omit it for the primary REGISTRATION_REQUIRED notification, which has
no rule. A status that reconciliation would skip — an unpublished or archived event, an
inactive registration, a participant who is no longer assigned, a status that is not
TODO or a deactivated recipient — has no notification to render and answers 404.

channel_ready=false means the recipient currently has no usable channel. That is not an
error of the preview: it is precisely what the administrator needs to see.
get.summary: Render a notification without sending it

404.description: nothing to render, or a foreign rule

get.description: All events with filters by state, participant and date range.

Search by display_name and normalised email to pick participants.
Only minimal fields are returned; credentials and channel data are withheld.

delete.description:
Removes credentials and delivery channels, anonymises the name and email.
Participation references and audit entries are preserved.

post.description: Restores access. Previously cancelled notifications are not revived.
Revokes sessions, removes the Telegram link and moves pending notifications to CANCELLED.

get.description: Issues the token in a cookie and in the response body. Every mutating request must send it in the X-CSRF-Token header.

post.description: Promotes pending_email to the primary address. Until confirmation, sign-in uses the previous address.

Issues a 15-minute access token and a rotating 30-day refresh token in HttpOnly cookies.
Rate limit: 10 attempts per 15 minutes per IP and email pair.
post.summary: Sign in with email and password

401.description: invalid credentials or a deactivated account

post.description: Revokes the refresh token of the current session and clears the cookies.
post.summary: Sign out of the current session

post.description: Revokes every active session of the user.
Issues a one-time token valid for 30 minutes. The response does not disclose whether an account exists.
After a password change every active session of the user is revoked.
Rotates the refresh token. Reusing a revoked token revokes the entire session chain.

Creates an account, sends a confirmation email valid for 24 hours and opens a session.
Sign-in is allowed before the address is confirmed; product email notifications are not.
If invite_token is supplied, the invite is accepted in the same transaction.

409.description: email or nickname is already taken

post.description: Consumes a one-time confirmation token valid for 24 hours.

400.description: the token is invalid or has expired

post.description: Rate limit: 5 requests per hour per IP and email pair. The response does not disclose whether an account exists.

get.description:
Serves an uploaded avatar by its server-generated key. The key is opaque and
unguessable; no client-supplied path ever reaches the storage.

Returns the owner's schedule as an iCalendar document (RFC 5545) with the
media type text/calendar. This is the only unauthenticated endpoint in the
system that returns personal data, and everything about it follows from that
(specification 5.6).

The token in the path is the whole credential: there is no session, no cookie
and no CSRF check, because a calendar client sends none of them. The address is
fetched by Google, Apple or Microsoft servers rather than by the owner's
device, so it cannot be bound to a device or an address range.

The content is exactly what the owner sees in GET /me/schedule: their assigned
published events, the stages of those events and the registration deadline.
No other participant, no administrative field and nothing from the personal
layer appears here — widening the feed would be a privilege escalation through
a channel that has no authentication.

An unknown, malformed or revoked token answers 404, and so does the feed of a
deactivated account. A revoked token and one that never existed are
deliberately indistinguishable: 403 would confirm that the address was once
real. Rate limiting is keyed on the presented token, since there is no account
context until the token has been resolved.

Every published, non-archived event regardless of participation. The response
carries a dedicated payload that cannot include administrative notes.

The catalog requires a session: an anonymous request is answered with 401. An
unauthenticated listing would enumerate every event of the organisation together
with its organisers and prize pools, and the system is internal. It also carries
its own rate limit, counted per account, because a catalog page is heavier than
other reads: substring search, filters and the stages of the page.

parameters.description: Comma-separated origin filter. Omit it for the All view: RU and WORLD cover every event.
parameters.name: origin

parameters.description: Comma-separated format filter. OFFLINE and HYBRID also match an event whose own format is ONLINE when at least one of its stages is held in person.
parameters.name: format

get.description:
The same events the catalog listing returns, under the same filters and the same
sort, streamed as CSV instead of paginated JSON. Only the fields the listing itself
exposes are written: the export carries no administrative notes.

Like the listing it requires a session and is counted against the catalog rate
limit of the account. Rows are streamed as they are read, so the response is not
built in memory.

The `joined` column repeats the participation the listing shows. It says whether
the account takes part in the event, not whether anyone registered on an external
site: the system never checks that.

Participant role, computed state, stages, the nearest stage, registration status,
deadline and link. Administrative notes are withheld from the participant.

post.description:
Self-signup: the user joins a published event and supplies their own team role.
A meetup has no team role, so the field may be omitted; for a hackathon it is
required. A finished event cannot be joined: only an administrator may assign a
participant after the fact.

400.description: a hackathon requires a team role

409.description: already a participant, or the event has finished

get.description:
Every link attached to the event: rules, chat, submission form, dataset,
judging criteria and the rest. Pinned links come first, then the explicit
sort order.

A link carrying stage_id belongs to that stage and is meant to surface while
the stage runs rather than for the whole event. The system never follows a
link: no title, favicon or availability is fetched from the address, so an
address supplied here can never make the server call out (plan IVa.4).

The scheme is not restricted to HTTPS (specification 5.1): a plain http
address, an internal host or a tg:// address is stored as given. The scheme
must be on the accepted list: http, https, ftp, ftps, mailto, tel, tg,
matrix, webcal, irc, ircs and xmpp. Anything else is rejected, so a scheme
that executes in the browser or hands the address to an operating system
handler can never be stored. The client marks a non-HTTPS link but never
blocks it.

404.description: the event is not visible to the caller

post.description:
Attaches a link to the event or, when stage_id is given, to one of its stages.
A stage belonging to another event is rejected: the composite foreign key
(stage_id, event_id) makes the mismatch impossible to store.

The canonical registration address stays in Registration.url because it takes
part in notification content versioning (specification 7); a REGISTRATION link
here only displays that same value.

400.description: bad address, executable scheme or a foreign stage

403.description: only an administrator edits event links

409.description: the link limit for the event is reached

delete.description: Deletes one link of the event. The action is recorded in the audit log.

patch.description:
Edits one link of the event. Moving a link to a stage of another event is
rejected the same way as on creation.

post.description:
Participant self-report: moves their own TODO status to DONE. Available with an active
registration, an assigned participation and a non-archived event. The system does not verify the external site.

get.description: Available to an assigned participant for a published event, and to an administrator always.

post.description:
Creates an account for the invited address and opens a session.
Any other unexpired invites for this address are revoked in the same transaction.

get.description: Returns the address and expiry of the invite without disclosing any other data.

patch.description: The administrator flag, Telegram chat_id and password are not changed by this endpoint.
Changes one artifact of the caller, including the self-reported submitted mark.

404.description: the artifact belongs to another user

post.description:
Accepts a single image part named "file". The stored type is decided by the
file content, not by its name or declared type: only PNG, JPEG and WebP are kept.
A previously stored file is deleted once the new one is in place.

delete.description: Deletes the stored file and falls back to the initials rendered by the client.

get.description:
Events the caller saved for later, newest first. The payload matches the catalog
entry, so the same card renders in both places.

put.description:
Marks a catalog event as interesting without joining it. A bookmark is not
participation: it creates no assignment, no registration status and no
notifications, and an administrator does not see it.

Bookmarking twice is not an error — the operation is idempotent.

404.description: the event is not in the catalog

get.description:
Tells whether a calendar feed is currently issued for the caller and when it
was last fetched by a calendar client.

The address itself is never returned here. The secret exists exactly once, in
the response that issued or rotated it (specification 5.6.1): a feed URL is a
bearer credential, the database keeps only its hash, and an endpoint that
handed it back on demand would turn any read of this resource into a way to
recover it. A lost address is replaced by rotation, not recovered.
get.summary: State of the own calendar feed

post.description:
Creates the caller's calendar feed and returns its address once. The address
carries a secret of at least 128 bits; only its hash reaches the database.

One feed per account (specification 5.6.1). When a feed already exists the
call answers 409 rather than silently issuing a second address: rotation is an
explicit operation, so that replacing a feed is never something that happens by
accident to a subscription living in someone's calendar service.

The issue is written to the audit log — it is an account security operation of
the same kind as revoking a session — but neither the secret nor its hash is
recorded there.

409.description: a feed already exists; rotate it instead

delete.description:
Stops the caller's feed. Idempotent: revoking an absent or already revoked
feed answers 204 as well.

The row is not deleted — it keeps the token hash taken and records that the
address was deliberately revoked rather than lost. After this the address
answers 404, indistinguishable from one that never existed.

post.description:
Revokes the current address and issues a new one in a single transaction. The
previous address stops working immediately: every calendar already subscribed
to it starts receiving 404 and must be re-subscribed to the new address.

This is the response to a leaked feed URL. Because the address is a bearer
credential stored on third-party servers, there is no narrower remedy: the
holder of a leaked URL cannot be identified or blocked individually.

get.description:
The built-in checklist templates. A template is a shared reference list, not a
personal record: applying one creates the caller's own tasks, and editing a
template afterwards does not touch tasks already created.

Titles are dictionary keys, not finished text: the client renders them in the
reader's language.

post.description:
Revokes sessions, removes the Telegram link and cancels pending notifications.
Reactivation is performed by an administrator.
The new address is stored as pending_email and becomes primary only after confirmation.

get.description:
Published events with an assigned participation: UPCOMING, ACTIVE and FINISHED.
Archived records are hidden by default and available through a filter.

The system event bus, not the notification queue of specification section 9. A row here
mirrors something that happened; it never competes with Telegram or email for delivery
and never enters the deduplication and retry machinery of a Notification.

The feed returns exactly two audiences: events addressed to the caller personally and,
for an administrator, events addressed to administrators. There is no way to read
somebody else's feed.

parameters.description: Return only entries the caller has not read
parameters.name: unread

post.description:
Marks the listed events read for the caller. An empty list marks the whole visible feed.
Identifiers outside the caller's audience are ignored rather than reported: the endpoint
must not become a way to probe which events exist.

requestBody.description: Identifiers to mark, empty for all

get.description:
The number the bell shows. Requested over REST on connect; the socket only sends the
delta afterwards, so the counter is correct even when the socket never opens.

What the caller says they submitted for the event: repository, video, slides,
demo stand or submission page.

The submitted mark is the participant's own word, exactly like the registration
status of specification 1: the system never checks an external site, so nothing
here is a verified fact.

post.description:
Records one artifact of the caller for the event. The link is only checked for
being a parseable address whose scheme is on the accepted list, so a scheme
that executes in a browser or reaches an operating system handler is rejected.

409.description: the artifact limit for this event is reached

get.description:
The caller's private links for one event, kept in a table of their own rather
than mixed into the event links. Separate storage keeps the permission check
simple: an event link is administrative, a personal link belongs to whoever
created it, and no query has to tell the two apart at read time.

Nobody else can read these links, an administrator included.

404.description: the event is not visible to the caller

post.description:
Saves a private link of the caller for one event. The address is validated the
same way as everywhere else: it must parse, and the scheme must be on the
accepted list, so a scheme that executes in the browser or hands the address
to an operating system handler is rejected. HTTPS is not required.

409.description: the personal link limit for the event is reached

get.description:
The caller's private Markdown note for one event. A missing note is answered
with an empty body rather than 404, so the editor opens on a blank page.

The server stores and returns the Markdown source and never renders it to HTML;
rendering belongs to the client. Nobody else can read this note, an
administrator included.

404.description: the event is not visible to the caller

put.description:
Stores the caller's note for the event; the endpoint suits autosave. Saving an
empty body deletes the record instead of keeping a blank one, so a list of
events carrying notes never fills with empty entries.

get.description:
The caller's self-reported result: how it went, and optionally a place, a prize,
a track and a note. The outcome is the participant's own account, not a verified
standing.

put.description:
Stores the caller's result for the event. The default is PARTICIPATED, and that
is a complete outcome rather than an empty one: most events end without a prize,
and a tracker that can only record wins makes the ordinary case look like a
failure.

A place may accompany only SHORTLISTED, WINNER or PRIZE — "first place" alongside
"took part" would contradict itself.

400.description: a place requires a placing outcome

get.description:
Three free-text fields the participant fills in after the event: what went well,
what did not, and what to do differently next time. A personal record in every
sense of specification 5.4 — only the owner reads it, an administrator has no
privilege here, and a foreign record answers 404 rather than 403.

An absent retrospective is returned as an empty one rather than a 404: the screen
that offers to write it must not have to distinguish "nothing yet" from an error.

404.description: the event is not visible to the caller

put.description:
Stores the caller's retrospective for the event. Every field is optional on its
own, but a retrospective whose three fields are all blank is equivalent to an
absent one and deletes the record — the same rule as the note in specification
5.4.3, so that a list of events with retrospectives does not fill with blanks.

The retrospective is a personal record: it never becomes a queued notification
and never reaches the audit log. Its reminder arrives as a system event on the
bus of specification 9.9, two days after the event ends.

get.description:
The personal checklist of the caller for one event. A task belongs to the
person who created it: the listing never shows anyone else's tasks, and an
administrator has no privilege here either (specification 5.4).

Personal records are outside the notification and audit domains: a task never
becomes a queued notification and never reaches the audit log.

404.description: the event is not visible to the caller

post.description:
Adds one task to the caller's personal checklist for the event. The optional
stage must belong to the same event.

400.description: the stage belongs to another event

409.description: the task limit for this event is reached

post.description:
Creates the caller's tasks from a template in one action. Due dates are counted
from the event start using the offset of each template item, so a negative
offset means "before the start".

A template item whose title already exists among the caller's tasks for this
event is skipped rather than duplicated, and the per-item outcome is reported
line by line, so applying the same template twice changes nothing.

get.description:
A read model over what the caller already accumulated: the events they were
assigned to, with their team role, their recorded outcome, their artifacts and
the count of their tasks. It owns no tables and shows only the caller's records.

delete.description:
Deletes one of the caller's private links. Personal records stay outside the
audit log, so the removal is not recorded there.

patch.description:
Edits one of the caller's private links. Somebody else's link answers 404: its
existence is not disclosed (specification 5.4).

get.description:
What the system sent the caller and when: date, type, channel and a short
preview. Read-only and scoped to the caller by recipient — an administrator
reading this endpoint sees their own notifications, not anyone else's.

The preview is a short excerpt, never the whole payload. Specification 4 clears
payload_json after 90 days while the row itself must survive for deduplication,
so an older entry returns no preview and no event title and is marked redacted.
The screen is required to render that state rather than treat it as an error.

The links shown on the profile, in their display order. The kind of each link
is not stored: the client derives it from the address, so a new service needs
no migration.

post.description:
Appends a link to the end of the list. The address must parse and use http or
https; schemes that execute in the browser are rejected. The number of links
per profile is bounded.

409.description: the profile link limit is reached

put.description:
Takes every link identifier of the profile exactly once, in the wanted order.
A partial list is rejected, so a reorder cannot silently drop a link.

get.description:
Only assigned, published, non-archived events. Each event is a separate row,
stages are returned as intervals and the registration deadline as a separate marker.
registration_status is the participant's own self reported mark, never a fact the
system verified against the external registration site.

Every active session of the calling account: the device that opened it, the address
it was opened from, when it was opened, when it was last used and when it expires.
One entry carries current=true — the session this very request authenticated with,
determined by the session identifier inside the access token.

Only the caller's own sessions are returned, and only to their owner. The user agent
and the address are personal data of the account holder: no other account reaches them
through this endpoint, an administrator included. Revoked and expired sessions are not
listed — the endpoint shows what is live now, it is not a sign-in history.

delete.description:
Revokes the refresh token of a single session, leaving the other devices signed in.
Repeating the call on an already revoked or expired session succeeds as well.

The session must belong to the caller. An identifier of somebody else's session is
answered with 404 rather than 403: the very existence of another account's session
must not be disclosed. Terminating the current session is allowed and clears the
cookies of this response, which makes it equivalent to signing out.

The outstanding access token stays valid for the rest of its 15 minutes: revocation
ends the refresh chain, it does not reach a token already issued.

404.description: the session does not exist or belongs to another account

patch.description:
Gives the session a label of the account holder's choosing, so a list of look-alike
browsers can be told apart. The label is free text of at most 64 characters and it
is stored as written: the server neither interprets it nor derives anything from it.

Sending clear_label drops a label set earlier and leaves the session unnamed. A
request that carries neither label nor clear_label changes nothing and is refused,
so an empty body cannot silently erase a name.

The session must belong to the caller. An identifier of somebody else's session is
answered with 404 rather than 403, exactly as termination is: the very existence of
another account's session must not be disclosed. Naming a session has no effect on
its lifetime — it neither extends nor shortens the refresh chain.

404.description: the session does not exist or belongs to another account

get.description: The map binds an action identifier to a shortcut. An action missing from the map keeps its default.

put.description:
The whole map is replaced. Two actions may not claim the same shortcut,
and shortcuts owned by the browser or the operating system are refused.
put.summary: Replace your own keyboard shortcut overrides

409.description: the shortcut is taken or reserved

delete.summary: Reset every keyboard shortcut to its default

delete.description:
Removes one task of the caller. Personal records may be deleted outright:
unlike the administrative layer, they carry no retention obligation.

patch.description:
Changes one task of the caller. Marking a task done and undone are both plain
updates: the transition is reversible and produces neither a notification nor
an audit entry. A task of another user answers 404, never 403.

404.description: the task belongs to another user

post.description:
Returns a one-time deep link bound to the current user.
The chat identifier is set only by this flow.

get.description:
Protected endpoint. Requires an Authorization header with the METRICS_TOKEN bearer token,
when the token is set by configuration.

The rows an operator needs to tell a stuck queue apart from a busy one. The heartbeat
answers whether something is broken; this answers what exactly.

scope=failures lists terminal failures — FAILED after the four provider calls of
specification section 9.4.8 are spent, and UNDELIVERABLE when no channel was available
or every channel closed with a permanent error — each with the reason recorded in
last_error, the attempt count and the channels already tried.

scope=stuck-leases lists entries left in PROCESSING whose worker lease expired. That is
the same set the recovery task of section 9.4.9 returns to the queue; this endpoint only
reports it and recovers nothing. lease_overdue_seconds says how long the lease has been
overdue, which separates a worker that died from one that is merely slow.

The rows carry no payload_json, no recipient and no registration status: an operations
screen is not a way to read other people's notifications or assignments.

Last run times of the scheduler and worker, queue lengths by status
and the age of the oldest pending entry.

Served without authentication. A profile is visible only when its owner
turned visibility on; otherwise the response is 404, so that the existence
of a closed profile is not disclosed. Events are limited to published,
non-archived ones that the person allowed to be shown.
Checks that the database is reachable.

WebSocket upgrade. The socket is read-only: it carries cache invalidation addresses and
event-bus entries, never domain payloads. Data still arrives over the ordinary authorized
REST endpoints, so the socket cannot reveal anything a GET would refuse.

The handshake carries no CSRF header — a WebSocket handshake cannot set one — so Origin is
checked explicitly and a mismatch is refused with 403. SameSite=Lax does not cover a
WebSocket upgrade: without this check any site a signed-in user visits could open a socket
as them.

The connection is bound to the session rather than to the 15-minute access token, and is
closed when the session is revoked, the user signs out or the account is deactivated.

Teams the caller leads or belongs to, including the ones they were invited into
and have not accepted yet. A team the caller left is not listed.

post.description: The caller becomes the team lead and its first active member.

get.description:
Visible to the members of the team alone. A team the caller does not belong to
answers 404: the existence of somebody else's team is not disclosed.

patch.description: Restricted to the team lead. A member who is not the lead receives 403.

get.description: Every entry the team holds, each with its own roster and derived standing.

post.description:
Restricted to the team lead. Only a published, non-archived event of kind HACKATHON
accepts a team entry. The entry starts with an empty roster: the lead then draws a
lineup for this event from the team's active members, and the team's size limits
apply to that lineup, not to the whole team. Entering registers nobody: registration
stays the self-report of each member and the system never checks the external site.
post.summary: Enter a hackathon as a team

get.description:
`registered` is derived, never stored: the team counts as registered once the number
of roster members who reported their own registration reaches the event's
`team_size_min`. Team members outside this event's roster do not count towards it.
An event without `team_size_min` has no threshold and is never derived registered.
Every count is a self-report, not a verified fact.

put.description:
Restricted to the team lead. The lineup for an event is drawn from the team's active
members and may be smaller than the team. The event's `team_size_max` caps the
lineup and a further addition is refused with `roster_full`; `team_size_min` is only
the threshold of the derived registered state and never blocks an addition, so an
under-filled lineup is allowed while it is being assembled.
put.summary: Put a team member on the event roster

delete.description:
Restricted to the team lead. The member stays in the team; only this event's lineup
loses them. Their personal registration status on the event is left untouched.
delete.summary: Take a team member off the event roster

post.description:
Restricted to the team lead, and only for a member on this event's own roster. It
writes the same personal registration status the member writes themselves, so the
value stays a self-report relayed by the lead rather than a verified fact; the audit
